text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (Comesa) Secretary-General Bingu wa Mutharika has threatened legal action over his suspension from the body. He has threatened to sue Comesa should a commission of inquiry into allegations of mismanagement and misappropriation of funds find him innocent.
- The opposition Alliance for Democracy (Aford) party has gone to court to challenge President Bakili Muluzi's freedom to choose anyone as a cabinet minister.
- Civil servants previously given free telephone services in their homes will have to pay for them from April 1.

- Top members of the ruling United Democratic Front allegedly plotted the apparent fall from grace of Malawian born Comesa Secretary-General Bingu wa Mutharika after he indicated he would go into politics.
- Thieves broke into a Blantyre police station at the weekend and escaped with unclaimed lost property.
